models.title: Benchmark-relative active return
models.summary: The owner describes subtracting the FTSE benchmark return from each portfolio return to obtain excess returns.

relationship.original_equation: Active return = portfolio return − benchmark return
relationship.locator: Summary, value added and active return
relationship.translation_notes: Both inputs and the output are base-one dimensionless return fractions; a difference of 0.01 is one percentage point.

variables.definition: Portfolio total return over the specified period as a base-one fraction

variables.definition: Benchmark total return over the same period as a base-one fraction
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

variables.definition: Arithmetic difference between portfolio and benchmark returns
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: The two returns cover matching observation dates, reporting currency, total-return convention and appropriately selected benchmark.
Both inputs are comparable base-one simple period returns, not return levels or prices.
limitations: This is an arithmetic return spread, not the compounded wealth-relative return (1+portfolio)/(1+benchmark)−1.
Fees, taxes, cash flows and benchmark composition must be aligned before comparing performance; active return is not necessarily risk-adjusted alpha.
